sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Accretion & Homogeneous Phase**: The Earth formed approximately 4.5 billion years ago through the **accretion** of planetesimals, initially resulting in a largely homogeneous mixture of rock and metal.
• **Planetary Differentiation**: Heat from radioactive decay, gravitational compression, and meteorite impacts caused widespread melting, initiating **differentiation** where denser materials sank and lighter materials floated.
• **Density Stratification**: Iron and nickel sank toward the center to form the proto-core, while lighter silicates migrated upward to form the primitive mantle and crust.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The core-mantle boundary lies at a depth of roughly 2,900 km, representing the most drastic compositional and density transition within Earth's interior.

items.definition: The gravitational separation of Earth's materials based on density, where iron/nickel sank to the center and silicates rose.
The boundary between the lower mantle and the outer core (approx. 2,900 km depth), where S-waves stop and P-waves refract sharply.
The boundary separating the crust from the underlying mantle, marked by a sudden increase in seismic wave velocities.
The mechanism by which fluid motion in the liquid outer core generates Earth's magnetic field through self-exciting dynamo action.

items.title: Major Internal Discontinuities & Spatial Depth
items.content:
• **Conrad Discontinuity**: Transition between Upper and Lower Continental Crust.
• **Lehman Discontinuity**: Boundary between the Outer Core and Inner Core (approx. 5,150 km depth).
• **Repetti Discontinuity**: Boundary between Upper and Lower Mantle (approx. 670 km depth).

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Inability to drill deep (deepest borehole, Kola Superdeep Borehole, reached only 12.26 km); reliance entirely on indirect seismic evidence.
• **Policy Interventions**: Advanced computational geodynamics, neutrino geosciences, and high-pressure diamond anvil cell laboratory experiments.

items.title: Mnemonic for Discontinuities from Surface to Center
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: "**C**orn **M**akes **R**eal **G**reat **L**eaders"
• **Decoded Meaning**: **C**onrad, **M**oho, **R**epetti, **G**utenberg, **Lehman**.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly recalls the exact sequence of seismic discontinuities from the crust to the inner core.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Density increases progressively with depth, jumping abruptly at seismic discontinuities due to phase changes or compositional shifts.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that the inner core is liquid due to extreme temperatures. Remember that while the inner core is hotter than the outer core, immense gravitational pressure forces it to remain in a solid state.

Mains Value Addition: In GS-1 Geomorphology answers, explicitly link the 'Evolution of the Layered Structure' with the initiation of plate tectonics and Earth's magnetic shielding, which preserved the early atmosphere from solar wind erosion.

keyTakeaways: Earth's layered structure is the result of planetary differentiation driven by internal heat and gravity.
Indirect evidence from seismic waves (P-waves and S-waves) and major discontinuities define the boundaries of crust, mantle, and core.
The liquid outer core generates Earth's magnetic field, while the solid inner core represents the ultimate stage of density stratification.
